findings.evidence: Test: 'stepper(maxwell, fields, courant, t_const); assert np.allclose(check_constraint(maxwell), target)'. The frozen targets (3.969964100680549, 3.642146197746812, 6.117107650049737) do NOT equal the constraint of the evolved fields at t=0.2. Reproduced exactly only when maxwell.E_* holds the SECOND ICN INTERMEDIATE STAGE of the last substep (f2 = fields + k2*dt, the argument of the last derivatives() call): f2-state constraint = 3.969964100681 == target (all 3 tests, to 1e-12). The natural implementation in which stepper stores the final evolved fields into the object gives 3.976748296795863 (rel. diff 1.7e-3 -> AssertionError); a side-effect-free implementation leaves maxwell.E_* = 0 and gives 0.0. Meanwhile step 13.13's targets match the FINAL evolved fields exactly (3e-15) and a stepper-stores-f2 implementation FAILS 13.13 (rel. err up to 0.155). So passing both 13.12 and 13.13 requires replicating gold's exact undocumented side-effect split: derivatives() writes its `fields` argument into the maxwell object, stepper does NOT write the final fields, and integrate() writes final fields before calling check_constraint (this exact arrangement verified to pass 13.12+13.13+13.15). No prompt or docstring mentions derivatives() mutating the object; 13.11's spec says stepper 'Returns the updated simulation time and the updated fields'. The 13.12 target therefore corresponds to no specification-compliant state.
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate the 13.12 targets from the final evolved fields (i.e., have the test do fields = stepper(...)[1]; maxwell.E_x..E_z = fields[0:3] before check_constraint), or change the test to pass the evolved fields explicitly: check_constraint after assigning the returned fields to the object. Alternatively state in 13.9's prompt that derivatives() must store its input fields into the Maxwell object and in 13.11 that stepper must not store the final fields.

findings.evidence: Prompt only says: 'across the z=0 plane, please apply mirror symmetry and for x =0 or y = 0 plane, please apply cylindrical symmetry.' The targets require the exact per-field parity table E_x_dot,A_x_dot:(+1,-1,+1); E_y_dot,A_y_dot:(-1,+1,+1); E_z_dot,A_z_dot:(+1,+1,-1); phi_dot:(-1,-1,+1) (extracted empirically from the inner-face values of the h5 targets). These parities are properties of the specific azimuthal/toroidal dipole configuration that is only revealed at step 13.14; at 13.9 nothing states the field is toroidal, and the naive readings (vector normal component odd under its own reflection, scalar phi even: (+1,+1,+1)) give different face values and fail -- tests use generic non-symmetric fields (e.g. fields=(x,y,z,...,phi=1)) so the factors directly determine pass/fail. phi's odd-odd-even parity is especially unguessable (a scalar under 'cylindrical symmetry' would naturally be even). Additionally the BC application ORDER is unstated but scored: symmetry first then outgoing_wave passes (max resid 1e-15); outgoing_wave first then symmetry fails (maxdiff up to 3.94).
findings.suggested_fix: State the parity table explicitly in the 13.9 prompt (or state that the fields are azimuthal E=E_phi(rho,z)*phi_hat with A toroidal and phi odd under x- and y-reflection), and state that the symmetry (inner) condition is applied before the outgoing-wave (outer) condition.

findings.evidence: function_header docstring: 'constraints : list of tuples -- A list of tuples where each tuple contains the time and the corresponding constraint violation value at that time step.' problem_io says the same. But the h5 targets are 1-D float arrays of constraint VALUES only (shapes (10,),(10,),(10,),(20,)). A docstring-faithful return of [(t1,c1),...] raises 'ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (10,2) (10,)' inside np.allclose and is scored as failure even with perfectly correct values (verified). The prompt body text ('The function should return the constraint violation at each time step') matches the target, contradicting the docstring.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the docstring and problem_io to: 'constraints : 1D numpy array of the constraint violation at each t_check interval (no t=0 entry)'. Alternatively regenerate targets as (n,2) arrays of (time, value) pairs.

findings.evidence: Prompt: 'uses courant number to control the substep size to ensure stability' -- the substep policy is not specified. Targets (t_const=0.2, courant=0.5, delta=2/48 -> courant*delta=0.0208333, t_const/dt=9.6) match ONLY the floor+remainder policy: 9 full substeps of courant*delta followed by one remainder substep of 0.0125 (maxdiff 3.2e-14). The equally standard uniform policy n=ceil(t_const/(courant*delta))=10, dt=t_const/n=0.02 gives maxdiff 1.9e-2 and fails all 3 tests (verified). Both policies satisfy the Courant bound and the ICN scheme given in the background.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify in the prompt: 'take substeps of size delta_t = courant*delta, with a final smaller substep so that the integration lands exactly on t + t_const'.

findings.evidence: Background gives only the continuum condition 'partial_t psi = -psi/r - l^i partial_i psi'. The frozen targets require a specific discretization: evaluate the full-array step-13.1 operator partial_derivs_vec(f, delta) (2nd-order one-sided at every grid boundary, centered elsewhere) and overwrite exactly the three outer faces with -(f + x*dx + y*dy + z*dz)/r, leaving inner faces and interior untouched (reproduced to 5.7e-13 on all 3 tests). Plausible correct alternatives fail: 1st-order backward normal derivative gives max abs deviation 8.9e-2; all-backward differences 2.4e-1; r*f-advection forms 6e-2..3e-1 (all >> allclose tol). Mitigating: reusing the previously-built partial_derivs_vec is the most natural implementation in this cumulative-code setting, which is why this is rated medium confidence rather than high.
findings.suggested_fix: State in the prompt: 'use the partial derivative operator from step 13.1 to evaluate the spatial derivatives, and apply the condition psi_dot = -(psi + x dx psi + y dy psi + z dz psi)/r on the three outer faces only'.

findings.evidence: Docstring: 'the array containing the constraint violation on each time grid spaced by t_check'. Targets have exactly 10 entries for t_max=1, t_check=0.1, i.e. checkpoints at t=0.1..1.0 with NO t=0 entry. An implementation that also records the initial (t=0) constraint returns 11 values and fails with a broadcast error. The step-then-record loop is the more natural reading, and the test's own initialize() already calls check_constraint at t=0 outside integrate, hinting it is not part of the record; hence minor.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the docstring: 'the first recorded value is at t = t_check; the initial (t=0) constraint is not included'.

findings.evidence: Prompt formula 'E_phi = -8 A (r sin(theta)/lambda^2) exp(-(r/lambda)^2)' contains free parameters A and lambda whose values are never given in the prompt, docstring, or main description. The targets encode A=1, lambda=1. Since initialize(maxwell) takes no other arguments, unity is the only sensible default, but it is still an unstated choice a solver must make.
findings.suggested_fix: State 'with amplitude A=1 and width lambda=1' in the 13.14 prompt.

overall_assessment: Steps 13.1-13.7, 13.10 and 13.14 are clean and fairly scored, and the officially-skipped 13.6 is neutralized by the harness injecting the gold class. However, the back half of the problem is heavily convention-trapped: 13.8, 13.9 and 13.11 are each solvable only by guessing an unstated discretization/parity/substep choice (every plausible alternative was verified to fail the frozen targets), 13.15's documented return type contradicts its target, and 13.12 is effectively unpassable because its target encodes an intermediate Runge-Kutta stage left in the object by an undocumented side effect of the gold code -- a requirement that directly conflicts with the implementation that 13.13's targets reward. GPT-5's 5/15 on this problem is consistent with these traps. As-is, scores on steps 13.8-13.15 measure convention-guessing more than scientific-coding competence; 13.12 should be considered broken until its target is regenerated from the final evolved state.
